Entries.Text: Find groups, fields and values in the selected file by their names and values. Fill in any of the inputs: empty ones are ignored, and the rest must all match. The deepest input given decides what is found: groups, fields, or the values of fields. Click a result to jump to it.

Find files, groups, fields and values in every file of the project by their names and values. Fill in any of the inputs: empty ones are ignored, and the rest must all match. The deepest input given decides what is found: files, groups, fields, or the values of fields. Click a result to open its file and jump to it.
Search the whole of the selected file, or only the selected group or field.
Matches the file name or alias.
Matches the internal or annotated name of a group.
Matches the internal or annotated name of a field.

Matches the value rows of fields: their value, ID or time of day, as chosen on the left. A value also matches by the name of its enum option. Vectors and colours are written as numbers split by commas, colours as R, G, B, A.
Which part of a value row the value is matched against.
The value contains the text. With Exact Match, it must equal it, and numbers are compared as numbers.
The value equals the input. Numbers are compared as numbers, so 1 finds 1.0. A vector or colour equals a list of the same count of numbers, or a single number that any of its components equals.
The value doesn't equal the input.
The value is less than the number. For a vector or colour, any of its components.
The value is less than or equal to the number. For a vector or colour, any of its components.
The value is greater than the number. For a vector or colour, any of its components.
The value is greater than or equal to the number. For a vector or colour, any of its components.
The value is between the two numbers, inclusive. For a vector or colour, any of its components.
The range, inclusive. Either end can be left empty.
How the inputs are matched, and the results listed.
Inputs must equal the text rather than be contained in it. Numbers are compared as numbers, so 1 finds 1.0.
List only the first result of each value found, to see which values are in use.
Run the search, or start over.
Runs the search. Leaving an input after changing it, or pressing Enter in it, does the same.
Empties the inputs and the results.
The search runs in the background. Results are listed as they are found.
Stops the search. The results found so far are kept.
Click a result to jump to it. The filter narrows the list down without searching again.
Over {0} results; only the first {0} are shown. Narrow the search to see the rest.
Finds these results again in the Mass Edit, to edit, delete or duplicate all of them at once.
The search result no longer exists. Search again.
